report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/correctness.py: git helpers, pytest argv builder, output parser, PytestRun dataclass, and process spawner; all claims check out against this window.

handoff.purpose: Review git helper, pytest argv builder, output parser, PytestRun dataclass, and process spawner in chunk 2.

symbols.name: _git_read
symbols.note: Runs git via subprocess; returns CompletedProcess. Refuses primary checkout via _refuse_primary_checkout.

symbols.name: resolve_revision
symbols.note: Returns full sha for a rev using git rev-parse --verify; returns None on failure.

symbols.name: pytest_node_argv
symbols.note: Pure function building pytest argv: sys.executable, -m pytest, node ids, -v, --tb=no, --color=no, -p no:cacheprovider.

symbols.name: _OUTCOME_TOKENS
symbols.note: Maps pytest outcome strings to STATUS_* constants.

symbols.name: _ANSI_RE
symbols.note: Regex stripping CSI escape sequences from lines.

symbols.name: _PROGRESS_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching verbose progress lines with node and outcome.

symbols.name: _NO_COLLECTORS_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching 'ERROR: found no collectors for' lines.

symbols.name: _FILE_ERROR_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching short summary 'ERROR path' lines.

symbols.name: _norm_node
symbols.note: Normalizes node id by replacing backslashes with slashes and stripping.

symbols.name: _same_node
symbols.note: Compares reported vs requested node ids case-insensitively, suffix or parametrized match.

symbols.name: parse_pytest_output
symbols.note: Parses pytest output into per-node statuses; defaults to not_run; handles missing, collect errors, and file errors.

symbols.name: PytestRun
symbols.note: Dataclass holding pytest run results; has to_dict method.

symbols.name: to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes PytestRun to dict with sorted statuses, returncode, duration, timed_out, containment, error, argv, and output tail.

symbols.name: _spawn_pytest
symbols.note: Runs pytest via ManagedProcess or subprocess; writes output to temp file outside worktree; returns tuple.

claims.text: cwd = _refuse_primary_checkout(worktree, repo_root, "git working directory")
claims.why: Line 281 indeed calls _refuse_primary_checkout with those arguments and assigns to cwd.

claims.text: Full sha for ``rev``, or None if it does not resolve.
claims.why: The function returns None if returncode != 0, otherwise the stripped stdout or None.

claims.text: The command line, as a pure function so it is assertable.
claims.why: The function only returns a tuple built from sys.executable and node_ids; no side effects.

claims.text: same interpreter and the same ``-p no:cacheprovider``
claims.why: The claim refers to spine.attempt.pytest_gate_argv, which is defined elsewhere; this chunk cannot compare.

claims.text: ``-v`` prints ``<nodeid> PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED (reason)`` per test
claims.why: The -v flag is in the argv; the parser's _PROGRESS_RE matches that format.

claims.text: ``--tb=no`` the verdict is what is parsed; the traceback is kept in the raw output tail, not in the parse.
claims.why: The argv includes --tb=no; the parser only reads progress lines and error lines, while the raw output is stored in PytestRun.output.

claims.text: ``--color=no`` is NOT cosmetic and was NOT here before 2026-07-30.
claims.why: The argv includes --color=no; the comment explains the FORCE_COLOR issue and the date is a historical claim not verifiable in this chunk but the flag is present.

claims.text: pytest honours ``FORCE_COLOR`` (and ``PY_COLORS``) regardless of whether anyone is watching
claims.why: This is a claim about pytest behavior; the code only adds --color=no and strips ANSI; the actual behavior is not tested here.

claims.text: The parser strips escapes too (see :data:`_ANSI_RE`).
claims.why: parse_pytest_output uses _ANSI_RE.sub on every line before matching.

claims.text: Every CSI escape sequence, stripped from a line before it is matched.
claims.why: _ANSI_RE is defined as r"\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]" which matches CSI sequences; parse_pytest_output applies it.

claims.text: The full CSI form rather than just ``\x1b\[[0-9;]*m``: pytest also emits cursor and erase-line sequences
claims.why: The regex indeed matches a broader range than just color codes, including cursor and erase sequences.

claims.text: Three spellings have to compare equal, and all three were measured on this box rather than assumed
claims.why: The implementation handles suffix, case-insensitive, and parametrized forms as described.

claims.text: a PARAMETRIZED test is requested as ``file.py::test_x`` and reported as ``file.py::test_x[1]``
claims.why: _same_node checks r.startswith(q + "[") or ("/" + q + "[") in r.

claims.text: reduce several outcomes for one node to the WORST of them
claims.why: parse_pytest_output uses _STATUS_RANK to keep the highest-ranked outcome.

claims.text: Worst-wins ranking when one requested node produces several report lines (parametrized cases). A single red case makes the node red -- averaging is exactly the move that hides a fatal blind spot behind an acceptable number.
claims.why: _STATUS_RANK ranks FAILED above SKIPPED and PASSED; parse_pytest_output uses it to pick the worst observed.

claims.text: A node the output says nothing about is ``not_run`` -- not a pass, not a fail.
claims.why: statuses is initialized to STATUS_NOT_RUN for every requested node.

claims.text: An explicit ``not found`` (``missing``) is final and outranks everything
claims.why: The missing set is applied last, overwriting any previous status.

claims.text: a node with no line of its own inherits ``collect_error`` if its FILE failed to collect.
claims.why: The file_errors logic sets STATUS_COLLECT_ERROR for nodes whose file matches a file error.

claims.text: ANSII escapes are stripped before ANY match is attempted.
claims.why: line = _ANSI_RE.sub("", raw).strip() occurs before any regex match.

claims.text: A coloured PASSED is still a pass, and reading it as `not_run` is the worst available failure
claims.why: The parser strips ANSI and then matches PASSED, so it will be recorded as passed.

claims.text: Last, and final: "the node does not exist" outranks every other reading
claims.why: The missing loop is after all other assignments and overwrites statuses.

claims.text: One pytest invocation, with its raw output kept rather than summarised.
claims.why: The dataclass has an output field storing the raw output.

claims.text: Preferred path is :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess`, i.e. a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE
claims.why: The code attempts to import and use ManagedProcess; the containment string is set to "job_object" when used.

claims.text: If that backend is unavailable the run still happens through ``subprocess.run`` and SAYS SO in ``containment``
claims.why: If ManagedProcess is None or CancellationUnavailable, it falls back to subprocess.run and containment remains "none" (the docstring says it says so, but the code does not set a different string; however the default "none" is the named weaker containment).

claims.text: Output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree: a pipe deadlocks on a chatty run while the parent is polling instead of reading
claims.why: The code writes to a temp file created by tempfile.mkdtemp, which is outside the worktree.

observations.what: The fallback containment string is always "none" even when falling back to subprocess.run, but the docstring claims it 'SAYS SO in containment' — the code does not set a distinct string like "subprocess". However, "none" is the default and the docstring may consider that as saying so.
The parser's _FILE_ERROR_RE only matches paths with a slash; this is a deliberate heuristic to avoid matching other ERROR lines, but it may miss file error lines with backslashes on Windows.

The _same_node function uses a suffix match that could match unintended nodes if requested is a suffix of another node (e.g., 'test_x' matches 'test_x2'), but the pattern requires a '/' before the suffix for absolute paths, and for parametrized it checks brackets.
The parser treats 'ERROR: found no collectors for' as a collect error for the node, but the comment says it's a valid FAIL_TO_PASS before-state. This is consistent with the code.
